brand.tagline: Golden-flower sticky rice from the Hải Dương countryside

products.name: Yellow-flower sticky rice
products.description: Yellow-flower sticky rice grown, dried, milled and packed by the family in Duy Tân, Kinh Môn, Hải Dương. It cooks into soft, fragrant sticky rice with the taste of the countryside.
features: Fragrant, with the taste of home
products.cookingTips: [MẪU] Ngâm nếp 6 đến 8 tiếng, để ráo rồi đồ xôi khoảng 30 phút. Rắc chút muối và đảo đều giữa chừng cho xôi chín đều.

timeline.title: A farm supply shop at home
timeline.description: Since 2008, the family has run a shop that sells farm supplies and yellow-flower sticky rice seed to farmers in the area.

timeline.title: The first rice with the home village's name
timeline.description: With encouragement and support from the local farming cooperative, the family brought the village's yellow-flower sticky rice to market. The seed is chosen with care, and family members tend each field by hand. The cooperative gave advice, helped buy a small vacuum sealer and designed the bag. The first year packed 10 tonnes of rice, about 5,000 bags of 2 kg. The same year, the Hải Dương Department of Agriculture certified the producer as meeting food safety conditions.

images.alt: Food safety certificate of the producer, issued in 2021
The first 2 kg bag of Duy Tân yellow-flower sticky rice, 2021

timeline.title: A 20-tonne dryer and a new mill
timeline.description: As orders grew, the family invested in a paddy dryer that takes 20 tonnes per batch, a rice mill, and a vacuum sealer that packs 4 bags at a time instead of 1. That year, 30 tonnes of rice reached customers, about 15,000 bags. The drying and milling steps are in “A grain's story”.

images.alt: The rice mill and the paddy dryer in the family workshop

timeline.title: Neat square packs, on supermarket shelves
timeline.description: In 2023–2024, the rice moved to neat, square vacuum-pressed packs, each labelled by hand. Each year brought 40 tonnes of rice, about 20,000 bags, and the rice reached supermarket shelves.

images.alt: Rows of square 2 kg packs, each with a label stuck on by hand

timeline.title: A printed bag, 50 tonnes
timeline.description: The logo and product details are now printed on the bag, instead of the stick-on labels of earlier years. In 2025, the family produced 50 tonnes of rice, about 25,000 bags.

images.alt: A stack of Duy Tân yellow-flower sticky rice bags with the printed logo, 2025
